notebook.markdown:
Announcing the Metaculus Cup Summer 2026 With Dylan Matthews!

Each week we'll release a few questions covering current events. Forecast well to earn a share of the \$2,500 forecasting prize and a custom Metaculus-branded die. Contribute to the discussion to compete for an additional \$2,500 awarded to the tournament's top 8 commenters.

The first batch is:

* [What will be the relative rank of the weakest team to advance to the knockout stage in the 2026 FIFA World Cup?](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43328/lowest-relative-rank-of-knockout-team-2026-fifa-world-cup/) * [What will be the verdict in Musk v. Altman et al?](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43311/verdict-in-musk-v-altman-et-al/) * [Who will win the 2026 Colombian presidential election?](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43345/2026-colombian-presidential-election-winner/) * [Will another country announce they will quit OPEC or OPEC+ before September 2026?](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43333/another-opec-exit-announced-before-sep-26/) [](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43345/2026-colombian-presidential-election-winner/#comments) Questions are currently set to Upcoming. You can start forecasting now, and your predictions will be live as soon as questions open. (Scoring is determined only by the open period.) [](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43311/verdict-in-musk-v-altman-et-al/#comments)

The Community Prediction will go head-to-head against guest forecaster Dylan Matthews, the policy journalist who cofounded Vox's Future Perfect. If the Community Prediction is more accurate than our guest, an additional \$2,500 gets added to the forecasting prize pool.

Dylan is an associate program officer for the Abundance & Growth Fund at Coefficient Giving. Before that, he spent more than a decade as a policy journalist, most of it at Vox, where he was an original staff writer and cofounded Future Perfect to cover global health, pandemic prevention, anti-poverty work, and philanthropic ethics. Earlier, he covered tax, budget, and economic policy at the Washington Post's Wonkblog, with bylines in The New Republic and Slate.

The Metaculus Cup is also a great place to submit your own questions, helping the community grow and keeping Metaculus ahead of breaking news (find our question writing guide here). Write intriguing questions that attract forecaster engagement and you'll be in the running for our question-writing medals.

Join the tournament and learn more here.

notebook.markdown:
The [<u>Summer 2026 Cup</u>](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/metaculus-cup-summer-2026/) is in the books. 885 forecasters made 88,558 forecasts on 58 questions, and the community outperformed our guest forecaster, Dylan Matthews (more on that below).

Congratulations to our gold medal winners!

1. [benshindel](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/123595/)
2. [MaxA](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/174017/)
3. [Hippopotamus\_bartholomeus](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/247921/)
4. [MarcosO](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/241386/)
5. [exmateriae](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/119188/)
6. [tdeeno](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/292775/)
7. [Capital](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/279247/)

Along with their share of the forecasting prize pool, each of them wins one of our custom Summer Cup dice:

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/404d0eb8-d098-4830-9373-11e073281536.png)

Pro Forecasters [**exmateriae**](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/119188/) and [**benshindel**](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/123595/) are the first to have taken gold in all 3 Cup seasons (spring, summer and fall) and earn the large Metaculus rainbow die (the very first Cup had its own rainbow die, so they're the first to earn it under the seasonal format).

![](https://cdn.metaculus.com/user_uploaded/metaculus_die_dice.jpg)

Congratulations to both forecasters, that's a hard thing to pull off!

## **The community beat Dylan Matthews**

This season the Community Prediction went head-to-head against guest forecaster [<u>Dylan Matthews</u>](https://x.com/dylanmatt). The community [<u>won</u>](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43367/community-beats-dylan-matthews-in-summer-2026-cup/), which doubled the forecasting prize pool from \$2,500 to \$5,000.

Dylan held his own too, finishing with a bronze medal. Thanks to Dylan for playing and for bringing new forecasters to the Cup.

## **A first for bots**

Bots aren't eligible for prizes or medals in the Cup, but they compete on the same questions. This season Laertes and ManticAI finished 1st and 2nd overall, and FutureSearch finished 5th, which resolved our own question, [<u>Will a bot beat all humans in the Summer 2026 Metaculus Cup?</u>](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/43900/bot-superiority-in-summer-2026-metaculus-cup/), as Yes. The Economist [<u>wrote about it</u>](https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2026/09/16/artificial-intelligence-now-beats-some-of-the-best-human-forecasters) this week.

## **Commenting prize**

We also awarded a \$2,500 commenting prize to the top 8 contributors, judged on the quality and quantity of their comments. Congratulations to:

| Place | Name                                                                     | Prize |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----- |
| 🥇 1  | [WasteTimeContinuum](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/271410/) | \$600 |
| 🥈 2  | [MarcosO](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/241386/)            | \$500 |
| 🥉 3  | [exmateriae](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/119188/)         | \$400 |
| 4     | [Russell-viper](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/245211/)      | \$300 |
| 5     | [MaxA](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/174017/)               | \$250 |
| 6     | [matru](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/226104/)              | \$200 |
| 7     | [benshindel](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/123595/)         | \$150 |
| 8     | [jeffrey.liang](https://www.metaculus.com/accounts/profile/279973/)      | \$100 |
|       |                                                                          |       |

This was the busiest comment section we've ever had. Across the Cup, forecasters wrote **988 comments** and **881,753 characters**, somewhere between **550 and 700 pages of text.**

WasteTimeContinuum alone wrote **242,378 of those characters**. That's 150 to 200 pages, and the most any single forecaster has written in a Cup. He also collected 324 upvotes (second only to exmateriae's 340 in [Fall 2025](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/metaculus-cup-fall-2025/)) and 89 key factors.

MarcosO went the other way. He wrote only 33 comments, but these earned 16 "Changed My Mind" votes, the most we've ever seen in a Cup. The previous high was 12, from a forecaster who wrote 101 comments. MarcosO also finished 4th on the forecasting leaderboard.

## **What's next**

The [<u>Fall 2026 Cup</u>](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/metaculus-cup-fall-2026/) is now live, with *El País* data journalist [Kiko Llaneras](https://x.com/kikollan) as our guest forecaster. Can the community beat him too? [<u>Read the announcement</u>](https://www.metaculus.com/notebooks/45384/announcing-the-metaculus-cup-fall-2026-with-kiko-llaneras/) and [start forecasting](https://www.metaculus.com/tournament/metaculus-cup-fall-2026/#questions).
